bendme.headline: Lower your lid. Watch your desktop fold.
bendme.summary: BendMe turns a small movement of your MacBook lid into a live visual effect. Choose a style, start the effect and watch your screen change perspective.
bendme.audience: For MacBook owners who enjoy a playful desktop.
bendme.experienceTitle: Your lid becomes part of the effect
bendme.experience: You gently lower the lid; the desktop bends with it. Open it again to return to the normal view.
bendme.mechanism: A native Swift and Metal renderer uses screen capture and the lid sensor to draw the effect.
bendme.payoff: The effect is the point. It adds a small moment of delight to a familiar machine.
bendme.evidence: BendMe’s public code, built-in artwork renders and the existing MacBook demo are available to inspect.
bendme.barrier: Requires macOS 14+, Apple silicon and a compatible lid sensor. Screen Recording permission is needed. Pause in Appearance or the menu bar.
bendme.demo: Use the supplied lid demo and the two existing shader renders. The video shows physical lid movement; the artwork switch shows the visual states, not live tracking in the website.
bendme.gap: Screen capture stays on the Mac according to the project source. Compatibility should be checked on each supported model; do not promise the global pause shortcut works.
alternatives: A desktop that follows your MacBook lid.
A little lid movement. A visible bend.

resume-ai.headline: Turn scattered work notes into a resume draft.
resume-ai.summary: Resume AI helps you take the work you’ve done and put it into words. Start with your experience, work on a draft, then shape it around the job you’re applying for.
resume-ai.audience: For job applicants turning work experience into an application.
resume-ai.experience: You might have a few notes, an old resume and some projects you want to mention. Bring that experience together, then work on a draft you can edit until it sounds like you.
resume-ai.mechanism: AI-assisted writing helps organize your work and skills. You decide what belongs in the resume and how you want to say it.
resume-ai.payoff: It gives you somewhere to start when you know your experience but aren’t sure how to write about it.
resume-ai.flowTitle: Here’s what that could look like
resume-ai.evidence: The example on this page shows how rough notes could become a draft. Both versions use the same facts. It’s an illustration of the idea, rather than a response from the live app.
resume-ai.barrier: Before you apply, read through every claim and make sure it’s true. A clearer draft can help you explain your experience, but it can’t promise an interview.
resume-ai.demo: Keep the clearly labeled notes-to-draft illustration. It explains the intended input and output but does not prove the production AI workflow.
resume-ai.gap: User supplied resume-ai.winson.codes in the Vercel screenshot; end-to-end access, export formats, pricing and generation behavior have not been verified. Do not add a live CTA until checked.
alternatives: Your work experience, ready for a first draft.
Start your next application with the work you have done.

yabs.headline: Read your VPS benchmarks beyond the terminal.
yabs.summary: When you’re choosing a VPS, reading through benchmark logs can get repetitive. This visualizer helps you look through YABS results and compare what the machines measured.
yabs.audience: For developers comparing VPS benchmark results.
yabs.experienceTitle: Get a better look at the results
yabs.experience: Start with your YABS results and look through the measurements visually. That gives you another way to think about which server might suit your work.
yabs.mechanism: YABS runs the benchmarks. The visualizer presents those measurements so you can look through them without repeatedly scanning the terminal output.
yabs.payoff: You can spend more of your attention on what the results mean.
yabs.evidence: You can open the benchmark site and look through the public source code. The measurements come from particular tests, so the conditions behind each result matter too.
yabs.barrier: A benchmark gives you something to compare, but your own app may behave differently. Keep your workload in mind when you make the decision.
yabs.demo: Capture real YABS output beside the matching visualization. Highlight the same measurement in both so visitors can trace the source of a displayed value.
yabs.gap: No performance figures, supported import formats or workload wins verified for this rewrite.
alternatives: Compare the measurements behind your VPS choice.
Give YABS output a visual view.

arsenal.headline: Find the prompt you want to use again.
arsenal.summary: Sometimes you write a prompt you want to use again. Arsenal gives those instructions a place to live, along with the project context that makes them useful.
arsenal.audience: For developers who reuse prompts across their work.
arsenal.experienceTitle: Come back to the instructions you want to keep
arsenal.experience: Keep useful prompts with the work they belong to. When a similar task comes up, you can return to those instructions and adapt them instead of starting again.
arsenal.mechanism: Arsenal organizes prompts and reusable development instructions around your projects.
arsenal.payoff: The instructions you want to keep have somewhere to go after the conversation ends.
arsenal.flowTitle: Keep it, then come back to it
arsenal.evidence: You can take a look at Arsenal through the link on this page. It’s a project about organizing prompts and the development work they support.
arsenal.barrier: You’ll still need to give the AI the right context and check what it produces. Reusing a prompt doesn’t remove that part of the work.
arsenal.demo: Record saving an actual development prompt and finding it for a second task. Confirm the available controls before scripting the recording.
arsenal.gap: Sharing, search controls, integrations, sync, pricing and workflow execution have not been verified.
alternatives: Keep the instructions that worked.
Give recurring development prompts a home.

scatter.headline: Drop a ball. Follow every bounce.
scatter.summary: You drop a ball into the board and watch where it goes. Scatter is a browser-game experiment built around the fun of following each bounce.
scatter.audience: For people who enjoy short, playful browser experiments.
scatter.experienceTitle: The fun is watching what happens next
scatter.experience: Send a ball into the board and follow its path through the obstacles. Once it lands, you can try another drop and see what happens.
scatter.mechanism: The game uses physics to work out how the ball falls, hits the obstacles and reaches the bottom.
scatter.payoff: There’s a little anticipation in every drop.
scatter.flowTitle: Drop a ball and follow along
scatter.evidence: Scatter is a browser-game project I’m exploring. There isn’t a playable build linked on this page yet.
scatter.barrier: It’s a game experiment. This page doesn’t offer prizes or payouts.
scatter.demo: Record one uninterrupted ball drop in the actual build, from input to landing, with its real feedback. Show the board rather than a fabricated game screenshot.
scatter.gap: Public build URL and supported devices have not been verified for the portfolio.
alternatives: See where the next bounce takes you.
One drop, a board full of possibilities.

laundirii.headline: Follow a laundry order across three roles.
laundirii.summary: A laundry order passes through a few people. In LaunDiri, we brought the customer, courier and shop into one Android project to explore how those handoffs could work.
laundirii.audience: For people exploring coordination in a laundry service.
laundirii.experienceTitle: Think about everyone handling the order
laundirii.experience: A customer starts a request, then the courier and shop take part in getting it through. We wanted each person’s part to fit into the same service flow.
laundirii.mechanism: The app connects the customer’s request with the parts of the order handled by the courier and the shop.
laundirii.payoff: Everyone’s part in the service belongs in the design.
laundirii.flowTitle: From the customer to the shop
laundirii.evidence: LaunDiri is an Android project we built as a team to explore laundry-service coordination. The page shows the idea behind that work.
laundirii.barrier: This is a team project, rather than a laundry service you can book here. We aren’t offering delivery times or service coverage through this page.
laundirii.demo: Capture the same test order from the customer, courier and shop views. Show only handoffs supported by the actual app.
laundirii.gap: Current availability, exact role permissions, order status updates, team contributions and operational rollout need confirmation.
alternatives: One laundry request, more than one person.
Designing the handoffs behind laundry day.

techno-dynamic.headline: Explore course material through the questions it raises.
techno-dynamic.summary: Sometimes a lesson leaves you with another question. Techno Dynamic is a team project exploring how course material and AI-assisted content can help you keep learning about technopreneurship.
techno-dynamic.audience: For learners exploring technopreneurship course material.
techno-dynamic.experience: Open the course material, look through the generated content and follow relevant suggestions when you want to understand more.
techno-dynamic.mechanism: The platform brings course material together with AI-assisted content and suggestions based on frequently asked questions.
techno-dynamic.payoff: There’s another way into the subject when the first explanation leaves you wanting more.
techno-dynamic.evidence: We explored generated course content and question-based suggestions in this project. We haven’t established that it improves learning outcomes.
techno-dynamic.barrier: Generated explanations still need checking. They can support your learning, but they shouldn’t replace reviewing the material carefully.
techno-dynamic.demo: Record a real course section with its associated FAQ suggestion and resulting content. Use a verified lesson and retain any review notices.
techno-dynamic.gap: Live access, sources used for generation, educator review and specific team contributions need confirmation.
alternatives: A course page with somewhere to take your questions.
Bring technopreneurship material and questions together.

rad-ai.headline: Inspect an ultrasound classifier’s response to an image.
rad-ai.summary: Rad AI lets you look at what an image-classification model returns for an ultrasound research image. I built it as a research interface, not a tool for diagnosis.
rad-ai.experience: Give the classifier a suitable research image, then inspect the response. The output is an experimental result you can examine.
rad-ai.mechanism: The interface sends the image through the classification model and shows the result it returns.
rad-ai.payoff: You can follow the experiment from an image to its output.
rad-ai.evidence: This project explores ultrasound image classification. I haven’t supplied clinical validation or accuracy figures on this page.
rad-ai.barrier: Rad AI is a research prototype, not a validated medical device. It must not be used to diagnose someone or make clinical decisions.
rad-ai.demo: Use an authorized non-identifying research image and capture its actual model output. Keep the research-only notice visible. Do not invent confidence values.
rad-ai.gap: Model metrics, datasets, evaluation method, current availability and clinical validity are unverified.
alternatives: From an ultrasound image to an experimental prediction.
Put a classification experiment where it can be inspected.

jungle-guardians.headline: Give an animal classifier a picture to work with.
jungle-guardians.summary: Give Jungle Guardians an animal image and see what category the model predicts. I built it as a way to explore image classification through something familiar.
jungle-guardians.audience: For learners exploring computer vision with animal images.
jungle-guardians.experienceTitle: Compare the picture with the prediction
jungle-guardians.experience: Choose an animal image and look at the category the model returns. You can compare its answer with the picture and think about where it got things right or wrong.
jungle-guardians.mechanism: The interface passes your image to a classifier, then shows the category it predicts.
jungle-guardians.payoff: An animal picture gives you a familiar starting point for understanding a model’s response.
jungle-guardians.flowTitle: Choose a picture and see what comes back
jungle-guardians.evidence: Jungle Guardians is an interactive learning project about animal-image classification. I haven’t published an accuracy benchmark here.
jungle-guardians.barrier: The prediction can be wrong. The page doesn’t establish which species the model can reliably identify.
jungle-guardians.demo: Record a permitted animal image and the actual returned category. Include a real failure case if available, without inventing predictions.
jungle-guardians.gap: Supported categories, training data, evaluation and public access require verification.
alternatives: See what a model makes of an animal photo.
Explore animal classification one image at a time.

contact-manager.headline: Keep contact details ready to return to.
contact-manager.summary: Sometimes you just need to find someone’s details and keep them up to date. Contact Manager is a focused project for working with those records.
contact-manager.audience: For people maintaining a collection of contact records.
contact-manager.experienceTitle: Come back to the details you need
contact-manager.experience: Look through your contacts, maintain the stored information and return to a record when you need the details again.
contact-manager.mechanism: I used Angular for the interface and Supabase for the data side of the contact-management project.
contact-manager.payoff: Your contact records have a place you can return to.
contact-manager.flowTitle: Find a record and work with its details
contact-manager.evidence: This is a contact-management application project built with Angular and Supabase. I haven’t published a security or scale assessment here.
contact-manager.barrier: The project description alone isn’t enough to judge whether it’s suitable for sensitive customer information.
contact-manager.demo: Use fictional contact details in an actual build. Show browsing a record and a supported edit, then confirm the saved value before presenting that capability.
contact-manager.gap: Authentication, data access policies, supported edit operations, import/export and live availability need verification.
alternatives: Return to the contact record you need.
Give contact records a focused workspace.
